correctness.rationale: The fourteen facet halfspaces exhaust the nine-vertex full-dimensional convex hull because every one supports three independent vertices and a 3-polytope with nine vertices has at most 14 facets. Threefold rotation and horizontal reflection force any unique maximal inscribed or minimal enclosing ellipsoid to be a centered rotational spheroid. Horizontal facets impose b≤h, vertical normals impose squared horizontal radius A=3r²/[4(1−r+r²)], and strict slope slack equals r(2−r)²(1−r)/[4(1−r+r²)]>0; hence the John spheroid is feasible and optimal. The Loewner optimization of s^(3/2)/sqrt(s−r²), s≥1, changes optimizer at r²=2/3. Independent SymPy derivative and slack identities plus 5 reconstructed ConvexHull face patterns corroborate. H(r)=r⁴−2r³+3r²+r−2 is strictly increasing, giving unique distortion optimum r_J, while min(h,sqrt A) crosses at unique r_I. Checked the excluded r=1/2 combinatorial endpoint and contact change at sqrt(2/3).
